hint: I saw a case just like this yesterday and it turned out to be a normal tracing.

parsed.rationale: This is not a normal tracing: V1–V3 show QS complexes (loss of R waves, V4 has only a tiny r) with about 2–2.5 mm of ST elevation in contiguous V2–V3, which meets STEMI voltage criteria and points to an anterior infarct; left axis deviation is also present, and from the image alone a persistent ST elevation from an older infarct cannot be ruled out, so clinical correlation and serial ECGs or troponins are needed.
